coverage:
WHAT I DID NOT GET TO — read all of this as a real gap, not hedging.

(1) DYNAMIC-IMPORT EDGES ARE ABSENT FROM MY GRAPH. My cycle detection and orphan detection resolve static relative specifiers only. I enumerated dynamic imports by grep and found few (renderer/index.tsx:19 → debug-hooks, ProjectSetupTab.tsx:174 → classic-save, ipc-handlers.ts:82-83 → node builtins, 4 in core tests) and hand-accounted for each, BUT tab-activation/sprite.ts:104-110 claims export-sprite is pulled in by dynamic import() and my grep pattern did not match that call site — so there is at least one dynamic edge I did not locate. A cycle that exists only through dynamic imports would not appear in my count of 3.

(2) THE 273 renderer→core VALUE EDGES ARE UNAUDITED INDIVIDUALLY. I verified direction (core never imports up) but did NOT ask whether renderer modules reach past the intended seams into core internals — e.g. whether components import core/level-classic/s1-io directly instead of going through the adapter. That is a real ARCH question in my brief's spirit and I only sampled it.

(3) src/renderer/workspace (11 files) AND src/renderer/shell (23 files) GOT ONLY TARGETED READS. I read facet-tools/capability plumbing in adapter.ts, dirty-tabs.ts, dirty-snapshot.ts, project-open-guard.ts, session-lifecycle.ts (partially), tab-activation/sprite.ts and commands.ts because specific traces led there. I did NOT do a structural pass on the facet registry, LevelWorkspace, or the tab-activation subtree — the facet/capability system is arguably the app's second architectural seam after ProjectAdapter and I audited only the parts adjacent to my findings.

(4) DUPLICATE-IMPLEMENTATION SWEEP WAS TARGETED, NOT EXHAUSTIVE. I checked exactly the four the brief named (palette models — clean; tile decode — A11; canvasGeom/composer-math — clean, no canvasGeom exists) plus objects/rings serialization (found dead legacy, A6). I did NOT systematically hunt other candidates: collision models (core/collision + collision-block.ts + collision-cell-word.ts + collision-palette-organize.ts + renderer collision-overlay-scope), history implementations (core/editing has sprite-history.ts, classic-domain-history.ts, save-coordinator, plus renderer history-hub/history-factories — four-ish undo mechanisms I never compared), or the compression codecs.

(5) NO BUILD/TEST RUN. Per the pinned-tree instruction I did not run vitest, tsc, or a build, so every claim is static-read + graph analysis. Specifically: I did not empirically confirm that `new ImageData` throws under this vitest setup (I inferred it from vitest.config.ts having no `environment` and offscreen-canvas-stub.ts:16 conditionally defining the global), and I did not confirm the dead modules in A6 are absent from the produced bundles.

(6) src/core/agent, src/main/aether, src/preload UNVISITED beyond their import edges. The Aether protocol surface is a cross-tool contract per the suite docs and I formed no opinion on its layering beyond the shared→core inversion in A10.

(7) A3's remedy is a DESIGN OPINION about which I have low confidence on cost. I am certain about the evidence (adapter.ts carries both engines' types; there is no save on the seam) but I did not scope how much of the renderer would move if save went onto ProjectHandle. Treat the fix text as a direction, not an estimate.

(8) I did NOT verify that components/art vs art-shared vs art placement causes measurable confusion — I checked the census and the import fan-out and concluded the art/art-shared split is defensible (art-shared = pixel-editing primitives used by sprite AND canvas AND classic), so I made no recommendation there. The taxonomy findings I did file (A7, A8) are the two where I could point at a concrete cost."
verified_clean: src/core imports NOTHING from react, react-dom, zustand, electron, or src/renderer — exact count: 0 violations. Verified two ways: (a) grep of every import/export-from specifier in all 213 src/core .ts files, whose complete non-relative set is {vitest 66, node:path 7, node:fs 7, fs 6, node:zlib 4, zod 2, path 1} — all node builtins and all inside __tests__ only, zero in production core files; (b) a full relative-import graph over all 536 src files showing exactly one core→non-core edge, src/core/agent/validation.ts → src/shared/agent-protocol.ts (type-only). Dynamic import() in core is 4 occurrences, all in __tests__ (classic-tile-transform.test.ts:262-263, object-subtype-rules.test.ts:292/:305).

Cycle count for the whole of src/ is 3, and they are the same 3 with and without type-only edges (listed in A9). For a 536-file, 84k-LOC renderer+core tree that is a genuinely healthy graph — src/core is entirely acyclic, and the codebase demonstrably fights cycles on purpose (project-runtime.ts:2-3 extracted history-hub to break editorStore→project-runtime; tab-activation/sprite.ts:104-110 converted a static export-sprite import to dynamic for the same reason, with the type-only `typeof import` at :110 correctly noted as erased).

There is ONE palette colour model, not two. Every RGB↔CRAM conversion in the app funnels through core/formats/palette.ts decodeGenesisColor (:7) / encodeGenesisColor (:24): the renderer's palette-grid-model.ts imports and composes them (withChannel at :202-215, swatchCss at :219-222, lineWords at :225-227) rather than reimplementing, and core/art/palette-copy.ts snapColorToGenesis (:5) does the same. The only near-duplicate is the 3-bit quantiser (`to3` inlined at palette.ts:25 vs channelLevel at palette-grid-model.ts:190) — identical formula, both correct, not worth churn. The comment at palette-grid-model.ts:197-200 documenting a deliberately-omitted second clamp, verified by a planted violation, is exactly the standard this repo's guards should meet.

components/shared/ purity is a real guard, not a decorative one. shared-purity.test.ts:53 matches the SPECIFIER not the statement shape, so it catches `import`, `import type`, `export … from`, bare side-effect imports and dynamic `import()` in one rule; :47-51 documents that a double-quoted store import previously walked through an earlier single-quote-only version; :57-65 adds a non-vacuity case asserting the file list actually contains MapStatusBar.tsx and has length > 5. Exact input that makes it fail: adding `import { useEditorStore } from "../../state/editorStore"` to any file under components/shared. This is the model the missing core-layering guard (A2) should copy.

The engine-openness facade is well factored and honest about its own history. src/renderer/state/open-project.ts:1-12 records that four call sites once derived 'which engine is open' independently and two disagreed, then collapses them into openEngine()/openProjectDir()/openCapabilities()/openArtTiers(). Its consumers respect it: project-runtime.ts:143/:149/:159/:163 gate all four savers on it, shell/dirty-tabs.ts:38-44 preserves the classic-wins precedence. The two bypasses are dirty-snapshot.ts:28 and project-open-guard.ts:59 (reported as A5); everything else routes through the facade.

Engine branching in the renderer is modest and concentrated, not smeared: 32 total occurrences of engine discrimination across all of src/renderer excluding tests, top files being state/open-project.ts (6, by design — it IS the facade), workspace/level-presence.ts (4), shell/commands.ts (3), components/classic/ClassicArtToolDock.tsx (3). No component or facet is doing ad-hoc engine sniffing at scale.

The port/provider pattern is applied consistently for the surfaces it covers. providers/ holds matched per-engine implementations behind one component contract — chunk-grid-{aeon,classic}, palette-{aeon,classic,canvas}, map-status-{aeon,classic}, object-{inspector,list}-{aeon,classic}, properties-{aeon,classic} — and the consuming components in components/shared/ subscribe to nothing (enforced by shared-purity.test.ts). The port interfaces themselves (ChunkGridPort at chunk-grid-aeon.ts:138, PaletteGridPort at palette-grid-model.ts:236) are engine-neutral in their fields.

The sprite editor's aeon-store coupling does NOT produce a broken classic path, despite four components reading getCurrentZone(useProjectStore.getState()) with no engine guard (SpriteCanvasHost.tsx:45, FrameGrid.tsx:41, Timeline.tsx:51, SpritePaletteHeader.tsx:44). I traced the one scenario that would break — a document left at blankDoc's `paletteMode:'zone', zoneLine:1` (spriteStore.ts:226-227) in a classic project resolves to `[]` colours via resolveDisplayPalette (sprite-palette.ts:19) and would render every non-zero pixel MAGENTA at PixelViewport.tsx:136 — and it is unreachable: 'New Sprite…' is gated to aeon at shell/commands.ts:60 and lives under the aeon-only Object Library group (explorer-data.ts:162-172), while the classic entry point (the edit-art handoff) forces standalone mode at export-sprite.ts:525. PaletteEditor's standalone branch renders without a zone by design (PaletteEditor.tsx:64-66). Worth watching if 'New Sprite…' is ever ungated, but not a defect at this commit.

No geometry-helper duplication of the kind the brief suspected: there is no canvasGeom module in the tree at all, and components/classic/composer-math.ts (158 lines) is the single composer geometry module — its former packTilePixels re-export was already deleted and the migration is documented at classic-tile-buffer.ts:11-17, which I confirmed against the code (grep for packTilePixels returns exactly one definition, classic-tile-buffer.ts:57).

Path aliases are inert: `@core` and `@shared` are declared in vitest.config.ts:6-7 but grep finds ZERO import specifiers using either, repo-wide. Every import in src/ is relative, which is what makes the static graph in these findings complete. (Minor cleanup available: delete the unused aliases, or adopt them — but the current state is at least unambiguous.)

src/main is a genuinely thin layer with one core dependency, and it is the right one: src/main/guarded-write.ts:36 imports planGuardedWrite from core/project/save-guard — i.e. the main process consumes core's pure policy and performs the IO itself, which is exactly the split adapter.ts:6-8 describes. Everything else main touches is src/shared (11 edges).

findings.title: core/formats/sprite-mappings.ts is dead code AND the one core module that constructs a DOM ImageData
findings.claim: renderSpriteFrame (src/core/formats/sprite-mappings.ts:106) has zero callers anywhere in src/, yet it is the sole place src/core constructs a browser `ImageData` (line 127) and returns it in its public signature (line 111) — a renderer-type leak sitting in the layer that is supposed to be renderer-free.
findings.evidence: Import-graph pass over all 536 .ts/.tsx under src/ (relative-import resolver; repo has zero '@core'/'@shared' alias imports, so relative edges are the complete static graph) lists src/core/formats/sprite-mappings.ts among modules with no importer. Full-repo grep for 'renderSpriteFrame' outside .claude/worktrees/ returns only its own definition (sprite-mappings.ts:106), a stale doc reference (docs/specs/2026-06-16-sprite-mode-design.md:229), and a prose mention in a comment (src/core/art/classic-tile-buffer.ts:34). Signature at :111 is `{ imageData: ImageData; offsetX; offsetY } | null`; :127 is `const imageData = new ImageData(imgWidth, imgHeight)`. vitest.config.ts declares no `environment`, so tests run in node where `ImageData` is absent — the only reason a core test touching this would not throw is src/test/offscreen-canvas-stub.ts:16-33, which installs a global `ImageData` shim for every test file including core's. Failure scenario: someone revives this helper (the design spec at docs/specs/2026-06-16-sprite-mode-design.md:229 explicitly proposes refactoring it) and calls it from src/main or any node-side core path — `ReferenceError: ImageData is not defined` at runtime, with the whole test suite green because the setup file defines the global.
findings.fix: Delete src/core/formats/sprite-mappings.ts's renderSpriteFrame (and the file if parseSpriteFrame is also unused — verify its exports separately). If it is kept for the planned refactor, change the return type to a plain `{ data: Uint8ClampedArray; width; height }` so core never names a DOM type, matching the discipline stated in src/core/art/rasterize.ts:3-5 and src/core/level-classic/render.ts:5-7. Separately, scope src/test/offscreen-canvas-stub.ts to renderer tests only so it stops masking DOM leaks in core.

findings.title: The core-layering invariant has zero automated enforcement
findings.claim: "src/core imports nothing from src/renderer / react / zustand / electron" is the load-bearing invariant of this codebase's structure, and nothing enforces it: there is no ESLint config, no lint script, and no test that scans core's imports. The only import-layering guard in the repo covers a single directory (components/shared).
findings.evidence: package.json scripts (lines 6-12) are dev/build/preview/test/test:watch/gen:theme — no lint. `ls -a` of the repo root shows no eslint.config.js / .eslintrc*. The one source-scan import guard is src/renderer/components/shared/__tests__/shared-purity.test.ts:56, whose regex STATE_IMPORT is scoped to `state/` specifiers under src/renderer/components/shared only; it is a good guard (it even names its own vacuous-green failure mode at lines 57-65) but it says nothing about core. Grep for a core-layering test (`readdirSync` in a test asserting core imports, or the strings 'renderer-free' / 'no-restricted-import' in any .test.ts) returns nothing. The comment that states the rule is prose only: src/core/project/adapter.ts:6-8 ("Nothing in this module imports fs or Electron") and src/core/art/classic-tile-buffer.ts:13 ("core must never import the renderer — see the note at src/core/project/adapter.ts:87"). Failure scenario: any future edit adding `import { useEditorStore } from '../../renderer/state/editorStore'` to a core module compiles, tests pass, and the electron-vite main bundle either breaks at build time or silently pulls React into the main process — nothing in CI or the test run reports it.
findings.fix: Add a source-scan test modelled on shared-purity.test.ts (same walk + specifier-regex + the non-vacuous 'finds the files at all' case), asserting that no file under src/core matches /(?:from|import)\s*\(?\s*["'`](?:react|react-dom|zustand|electron)|["'`][^"'`]*\/renderer\//. Extend it with a DOM-global check (`ImageData|OffscreenCanvas|document\.|window\.` outside comments) — that catch is what would have flagged A1. Vet it with a planted violation in both quote styles, per the discipline shared-purity.test.ts already documents.

findings.title: ProjectAdapter's "engine-agnostic seam" carries both engines' concrete document types, and writes are not on the seam at all
findings.claim: core/project/adapter.ts is documented as "the engine-agnostic seam" (line 1) but imports both engines' concrete models (LoadedS4Config, S4Project, CollisionProfileSet at :16-18; LevelDoc at :213), names engines in its capability enum (`levels: 'chunk-hierarchy' | 'aeon' | null`, :135), and expresses ProjectHandle as a two-field grab-bag — `levels: ClassicLevelAccess | null` (:192) and `aeon?: AeonProjectData` (:197) — so every consumer branches on which field is populated. Saving is not on the interface at all: classic writes through `handle.levels.write()` while aeon writes through a direct core import with no handle involved.
findings.evidence: adapter.ts:16-18 imports LoadedS4Config / S4Project / CollisionProfileSet purely to type AeonProjectData (:177-186). ClassicLevelAccess (:265-308) is entirely classic vocabulary — DirtyDomains keys 'tiles'|'blocks'|'chunks'|'fg'|'bg'|'colind'|'start' (:226), EditableTileRange with animRanges (:260-263), reservedTiles (:307) — and four of its members are optional with comments saying "omitted by non-classic adapters", i.e. the interface is classic's shape with aeon opting out. ProjectHandle has no `save`/`write` member. Classic's save path: src/renderer/state/classic-save.ts:12 imports the adapter types, :188-192 reads `st.handle.levels` and calls its write. Aeon's save path: src/renderer/state/aeon-save.ts:7 `import { buildAeonSavePlan } from '../../core/project/aeon/save'` — no ProjectHandle anywhere in the file. Failure scenario (the concrete cost, not hypothetical): a third profile — or the planned per-act split — must either be shoehorned into ClassicLevelAccess's classic-named optional members or add a third top-level ProjectHandle field plus a third branch in every consumer, and it gets no save path from the seam at all because none exists there. This is why src/renderer/state/project-runtime.ts:141-167 has to register two independent savers keyed on `openEngine()` rather than one saver over the handle.
findings.fix: Move write onto the seam: add `save(dirty): Promise<WriteResult>` to ProjectHandle and have the aeon adapter wrap buildAeonSavePlan behind it, so project-runtime registers ONE project saver instead of the classic/aeon pair at :141-167. Then narrow the type leak — make AeonProjectData opaque to adapter.ts (a `data: unknown` or generic parameter resolved by the aeon module) so core/project/adapter.ts stops importing src/core/model/s4-types and src/core/config/s4-config. Rename `CapabilityManifest.levels: 'aeon'` to a structural value ('flat-sections' vs 'chunk-hierarchy') so the neutral enum stops naming an engine.

findings.title: aeon bypasses the adapter registry's open(): openProject() can never open an aeon project
findings.claim: Both adapters are registered (classic-bridge.ts:33), but the bridge's dispatch explicitly excludes aeon from `openProject()` — `if (match && match.type !== 'aeon')` at :68 — and routes an aeon match back out as `{ kind: 'not-classic', aeon: true }` (:72) so a renderer module calls `aeonAdapter.open(...)` directly instead (src/renderer/state/aeon-open.ts:22). The registry therefore only ever dispatches detect; the core `openProject` helper (adapter.ts:355) is dead for one of the two engines.
findings.evidence: classic-bridge.ts:33 registers `[s1Adapter, aeonAdapter]`; :67 `const match = await detectProject(fa)`; :68-71 opens only when `match.type !== 'aeon'`; :72 returns not-classic for aeon. src/renderer/state/aeon-open.ts:6 imports aeonAdapter and :22 calls `aeonAdapter.open(createIpcFileAccess(dir))`, :23 `const aeon = handle.aeon!`. useProject.ts:19-27 is the caller that re-routes: `outcome === 'not-classic'` → `openAeonProject(dir)`. Failure scenario: `openProject()` in adapter.ts:355 is documented at :353 as "the standard entry point for consumers", but in this app it is reachable only from classic-bridge.ts:69 behind a filter that excludes aeon. Any new consumer that follows the documented entry point (an agent tool, an Aether command, a headless test harness) gets `null` or a classic-only result on an aeon project, with the aeon adapter registered and matching. The non-null assertion at aeon-open.ts:23 is the other half of the same shape: the type system cannot say that an aeon adapter always populates `handle.aeon`.
findings.fix: Let the aeon branch go through openProject() too — classic-bridge.ts can return `{kind:'opened'}` for both types and let the caller commit an aeon handle via the same path, or (better, with A3) once ProjectHandle carries save, delete the `!== 'aeon'` special case at :68 entirely. At minimum, correct the docstring at adapter.ts:348-354 so it does not describe itself as the standard entry point while one engine routes around it.

findings.title: dirty-snapshot bypasses openEngine(), the module that exists to be the single answer to "which engine is open"
findings.claim: src/renderer/state/open-project.ts was created because "[f]our call sites used to derive this independently and TWO OF THEM DISAGREED" (open-project.ts:3-4), yet dirty-snapshot.ts:28 re-derives aeon-openness as `useProjectStore.getState().project !== null` instead of calling `openEngine()`. Since a classic open does not clear the aeon store, the two answers differ after an aeon→classic switch.
findings.evidence: open-project.ts:22-25 defines the precedence: classic wins, `openEngine()` returns 's1' whenever classicProjectStore.status === 'open', and its comment at :10-12 says "a classic open leaves a previously-resident aeon project in the store". src/renderer/state/classicProjectStore.ts:95-116 confirms it: `openDirectory` resets useClassicLevelStore (:101) but never touches useProjectStore. dirty-snapshot.ts:28 reads `project !== null` directly; :29 reads `useEditorStore.getState().dirty` with no engine gate. Today this is contained by luck of ordering, not by design: shell/dirty-tabs.ts:38 tests `s.classicOpen` BEFORE `s.aeonOpen` (:44), so the stale aeon flag loses the tie. shell/project-open-guard.ts:59 has the same unguarded read (`aeonDirty: useEditorStore.getState().dirty`) and its own :165-172 comment already names the resulting hazard — "a leftover aeon-dirty flag means the NEXT open sees phantom dirtiness 'Save & open' can never clear (re-runs the no-op savers forever)" — because project-runtime.ts:159 gates the aeon saver on `openEngine() === 'aeon'`. Failure scenario: reorder or add a branch in dirty-tabs.tabHasDirtyDot (e.g. handle aeon before classic, or add a third engine) and a classic level tab starts dotting off a stale aeon dirty flag that Save All is structurally unable to clear.
findings.fix: Change dirty-snapshot.ts:28 to `aeonOpen: openEngine() === 'aeon'` and project-open-guard.ts:59 to gate on the same, and subscribe useDirtySnapshot (:40) to classicProjectStore.status as well so the memo re-runs on the switch. The precedence then lives once, in open-project.ts, which is what that module was written for.

findings.title: ~640 LOC of unreachable modules in core and renderer, including a live-looking zustand store
findings.claim: Eight non-test modules have no importer anywhere in src/: src/core/formats/object-defs.ts (88), object-names.ts (134), s4-objects.ts (75), s4-rings.ts (30), src/core/import/color-quantize.ts (87), src/core/formats/sprite-mappings.ts (175, see A1), src/renderer/components/SectionList.tsx (77), src/renderer/state/toolStore.ts (22). toolStore.ts is the worst of them: a fully-formed zustand store for mirror/dither/pixel-perfect that reads as the tool-state source of truth and is wired to nothing.
findings.evidence: Import-graph pass over all 536 src files (relative resolver; grep confirms zero '@core'/'@shared' alias imports repo-wide, and the only dynamic imports outside tests are src/renderer/index.tsx:19 → debug-hooks, ProjectSetupTab.tsx:174 → classic-save, and src/main/ipc-handlers.ts:82-83 → node builtins, none of which reach these files). Per-name grep confirms: 'toolStore' has zero occurrences in src outside its own file; s4-objects/s4-rings/object-defs/object-names/color-quantize each zero; 'SectionList' appears only in a comment at src/renderer/workspace/facets/collision-facet.tsx:15. s4-objects.ts's binary packObject/serializeObjectList are superseded by JSON — src/core/project/aeon/save.ts:84-92 writes `.objects.json` / `.rings.json` via JSON.stringify. Excluded from this list deliberately: src/renderer/providers/properties-classic.ts, which is unimported on purpose and says so at :27-30. Failure scenario: a maintainer adding a mirror/dither option wires it to useToolStore (the obviously-named store), the UI reads the real state from spriteStore/canvasStore, and the setting silently does nothing.
findings.fix: Delete the eight files. If any are wanted as a record of a format (s4-objects/s4-rings pre-date the JSON switch), move them under docs/ or add a header saying they are unwired — but toolStore.ts specifically should go, because its danger is that it looks wired.

findings.title: components/ taxonomy is historical, not predictable: classic has a directory, aeon does not
findings.claim: 21 classic components live under src/renderer/components/classic/, but the equivalent aeon components sit loose at src/renderer/components/ root with no components/aeon/ — and seven of them are named so that nothing identifies them as aeon-only. Placement is therefore not derivable from the file's role; you have to read its imports.
findings.evidence: Directory census: components/classic/ 21 files, components/canvas/ 10, components/art-shared/ 11, components/shared/ 12, components/sprite/ 8, components/ui/ 8, components/art/ 5 — and 18 loose at root. Of those 18, these read the aeon-only projectStore/editorStore/s4-types with no classic branch (grep count of 'useProjectStore|editorStore|s4-types' per file): MapViewport.tsx 29, SectionGridNav.tsx 7, ArtBrowser.tsx 6, PaletteViewer.tsx 6, CollisionPalette.tsx 6, SectionList.tsx 4, MarqueePasteOptions.tsx 4 — plus the three explicitly-named Aeon*.tsx and ChunkLibrary.tsx. Measurable cost, not aesthetics: (a) `grep -rl aeon src/renderer/components` misses MapViewport, ArtBrowser, PaletteViewer, SectionGridNav, CollisionPalette and MarqueePasteOptions entirely, so "what is aeon UI" is unanswerable by search; (b) the misplacement is what makes the providers→components cycles in A9 cross a directory boundary that components/classic/ handles in-tree; (c) components/shared/ is protected by a real purity guard (shared-purity.test.ts) while the root has none, so an engine-specific component at root is indistinguishable from a neutral one.
findings.fix: Create src/renderer/components/aeon/ and move the eleven aeon-only files into it (MapViewport, SectionGridNav, SectionList — if not deleted per A6 — ArtBrowser, PaletteViewer, CollisionPalette, MarqueePasteOptions, RingPatternPalette, AeonChunkActions, AeonObjectInspector, AeonPropertiesPanel, ChunkLibrary), leaving genuinely cross-engine chrome (CommandPalette, ToastContainer, AetherStatus, AuroraMark, CollisionLegend) at root. Pure path churn, no logic change, and it makes the root directory mean "neutral chrome" — which is then assertable by extending shared-purity.test.ts's scan to it.

findings.title: Three unrelated meanings of "canvas" as sibling paths, one of which is a global theme module
findings.claim: src/renderer/canvas/ (aeon level-map renderers), src/renderer/components/canvas/ (the origination-canvas art document UI) and src/core/art/canvas-*.ts (the origination-canvas model) are three different subjects sharing one word. The collision is not merely cosmetic: renderer/canvas/canvas-colors.ts is the app-wide canvas theme (20 importers across sprite/classic/art/aeon) and has nothing to do with the four aeon renderers it sits beside.
findings.evidence: src/renderer/canvas/ holds exactly 5 files: TileRenderer.ts, SectionRenderer.ts, OverlayRenderer.ts, compose-nametable.ts (all aeon map rendering — SectionRenderer.ts:3-5) and canvas-colors.ts. canvas-colors.ts:1-7 declares itself "the canvas analog of styles/theme.css… the ONLY module (besides theme.css) allowed to hold raw hex", 187 lines. Its importers span every area: components/sprite/{Timeline,FrameGrid,SpriteCanvasHost}, components/classic/{BlockTab,TileTab,ChunkTab,ClassicLevelViewport,classic-overlays,composer-shared,composer-thumbs}, components/art/{TilesetPanel,ComposerCanvas}, components/art-shared/PixelViewport, components/shared/ChunkGrid, components/{ArtBrowser,CollisionPalette,CollisionLegend}, and components/canvas/{CanvasHost,canvas-pane-model}. The last two are the sharp edge: src/renderer/components/canvas/CanvasHost.tsx:14 reads `from '../../canvas/canvas-colors'` — a path that climbs OUT of a directory named canvas into a different directory named canvas, to reach a file whose subject is neither. src/renderer/styles/ exists and contains exactly one file, theme.css.
findings.fix: Move src/renderer/canvas/canvas-colors.ts → src/renderer/styles/canvas-colors.ts (it already names theme.css as its counterpart, and styles/ is where its counterpart lives), and rename the remaining src/renderer/canvas/ → src/renderer/map-render/ to match its four actual occupants. That leaves exactly one directory named canvas in the renderer, meaning the origination canvas.

findings.title: Three import cycles, all providers↔components or store↔store; benign today only because every use site is deferred
findings.claim: The static import graph has exactly three cycles: (1) components/AeonChunkActions.tsx → providers/chunk-library-import.ts → providers/chunk-grid-aeon.ts → back; (2) components/classic/ChunkPickerHeader.tsx ↔ providers/chunk-grid-classic.ts; (3) state/classicLevelStore.ts ↔ state/classicProjectStore.ts. None misbehaves today, but that rests entirely on every cross-edge use being inside a hook body or a `.getState()` call — one hoist to module scope turns a cycle into an undefined binding at eval time.
findings.evidence: Cycle detection over all 536 src files, both with and without type-only edges, yields the same three (a type-only edge cannot cause a runtime cycle, so the counts matching means all three are value cycles). Cycle 1: AeonChunkActions.tsx:4 imports chunk-library-import; chunk-library-import.ts:20 imports isBlankChunk from chunk-grid-aeon; chunk-grid-aeon.ts:26 imports AeonChunkActions. Cycle 2: ChunkPickerHeader.tsx:4 imports classicCanLoop from chunk-grid-classic; chunk-grid-classic.ts:28 imports ChunkPickerHeader. Cycle 3: classicLevelStore.ts:49 ↔ classicProjectStore.ts:35. Why they are currently safe, verified individually: the component bindings are consumed at `HeaderExtra: AeonChunkActions` (chunk-grid-aeon.ts:152) and `HeaderExtra: ChunkPickerHeader` (chunk-grid-classic.ts:159), both inside React.useMemo bodies (:138 and :140 respectively) that run at render, not module eval; isBlankChunk is called at chunk-library-import.ts:65 inside a function; the store edges are `.getState()` calls at classicProjectStore.ts:101 and classicLevelStore.ts:394/:736. Failure scenario: hoist any of these to a module-level const — e.g. `const HEADER = AeonChunkActions;` at chunk-grid-aeon.ts top level — and depending on which module the bundler evaluates first the binding is undefined, giving a silently missing header rather than an error. Worth recording that the codebase already fights this deliberately in two places: project-runtime.ts:2-3 (history-hub extracted "to break the editorStore→project-runtime cycle") and shell/tab-activation/sprite.ts:104-110 (a static export-sprite import replaced by dynamic import() specifically to avoid a cycle).
findings.fix: Break cycles 1 and 2 by inverting ownership: the header component should not be imported by the port that the header consumes. Either lift the two HeaderExtra components' shared predicates (isBlankChunk, classicCanLoop) into a leaf module both sides import, or have the facet — not the port — supply HeaderExtra. Cycle 3 is the more defensible one (two halves of one project's state); if it is kept, add the same explanatory header project-runtime.ts:2-3 has, so the next person does not 'fix' it by hoisting.

findings.title: src/shared depends on src/core, inverting the layer it is named for
findings.claim: src/shared is the module preload and main both consume, i.e. the bottom of the stack, but shared/agent-protocol.ts imports two core types — making core a build dependency of the preload bundle.
findings.evidence: Cross-layer edge census over the full graph: main→shared 11 edges, preload→shared 4, renderer→shared 15 — and shared→core 2, both from src/shared/agent-protocol.ts:6 (`import type { BlockDef } from '../core/level-classic/model'`) and :7 (`import type { S1ObjectEntry } from '../core/formats/classic/s1-objpos'`). Both are type-only, so nothing ships today; the inversion is structural, and it means the direction 'shared knows nothing about core' — which every other edge in the census respects — is already broken and would not be noticed if one of these became a value import. Note the mirror edge exists too: src/core/agent/validation.ts imports shared/agent-protocol.ts (type-only), so the two modules already reference each other across the layer boundary in both directions.
findings.fix: Move BlockDef and S1ObjectEntry's protocol-facing shapes into src/shared (or restate them structurally there), so agent-protocol.ts stops reaching up into core. Then the shared→core edge count is zero and can be asserted by the same scan proposed in A2.

findings.title: Two parallel 4bpp codec pairs for the same on-ROM format
findings.claim: The Genesis 4bpp tile encoding has two independent decoder/encoder pairs in core — parseTiles/serializeTiles (Tile{pixels} shape, the aeon path) and unpack4bppTile/packTilePixels (PixelBuffer shape, the classic art-edit path) — plus a third decode inlined in the dead renderSpriteFrame. Both live pairs are production code on opposite engines, so a nibble-order fix has to be made twice.
findings.evidence: Decoders: src/core/formats/tiles.ts:19 `pixels[row*8+col*2] = (byte >> 4) & 0xF`, src/core/art/rasterize.ts:150 `dest[o] = (byte >> 4) & 0xf`, and src/core/formats/sprite-mappings.ts:155 (dead, see A1). Encoders: src/core/export/tile-dedup.ts:126-140 serializeTiles and src/core/art/classic-tile-buffer.ts:57-65 packTilePixels. Both pairs are live and engine-split: parseTiles is called from src/core/project/aeon/load.ts:162 and :423, providers/chunk-library-import.ts:51, components/sprite/export-sprite.ts:194; serializeTiles from src/core/project/aeon/save.ts:138, core/export/index.ts:63, core/export/sprite-export.ts:100/:106. packTilePixels/unpack4bppTile serve the classic tile editor. Credit where due — src/core/art/classic-tile-buffer.ts:27-40 documents this exact inventory and its scope caveat, and my grep for nibble ops outside the compression codecs confirms the list is accurate rather than stale (the one thing it under-reports is that its third decoder is dead code). Failure scenario: the nibble order is pinned by a round-trip case in classic-tile-buffer's own suite and by rasterize.test.ts, but nothing asserts that parseTiles/serializeTiles agree with unpack4bppTile/packTilePixels — so a divergence between the two pairs (e.g. one 'fixed' for a Sonic 2 variant) would corrupt art on one engine while every test stayed green.
findings.fix: Cheapest correct step first: add one equivalence test asserting `serializeTiles([{pixels}]) === packTilePixels(pixels)` and `parseTiles(b)[0].pixels === unpack4bppTile(b,0).data` over random bytes, so the two pairs can no longer drift silently. Then, if unified, express Tile{pixels}↔PixelBuffer as a shape adapter over one codec and correct the inventory comment at classic-tile-buffer.ts:27-40 rather than leaving it to rot (as its own last line instructs).
